newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Lisbon bourse takes breather before results season.
newsitem.headline: Lisbon bourse takes breather before results season.

text.p: The Lisbon bourse is taking a breather, waiting for the stimulus of 1996 results before resuming its climb, dealers said.
"In 1996 the market rose mainly for macroeconomic reasons. This year it will grow for microeconomic reasons," said Nuno Thomaz, analyst of Lisbon broker Titulo Corretora.
Jose Freire of Espirito Santo Research (ESR) said: "The market needs a fresh stimulus -- 1996 results."

Analysts said the market had already discounted falling interest rates and progress towards meeting the entry targets for joining the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and would pay increasing attention to picking individual stocks.
"What we need now is 'stock picking' -- deciding which companies are set for growth," Thomaz said.
Analysts said they were unsurprised by the calmness of the bourse recently after its strong rise in the first three weeks of January. The market has risen 13 percent this year.
"The start of 1997 was very good. But how many companies have published 1996 results so far? Very few," said Freire.
Among 'blue chips" only Banco Comercial Portugues has so far released 1996 results. Banco Espirito Santo will issue 1996 results on Tuesday.
"After the strong rise at the start of the year, it is natural that the market should calm down a little," said Thomaz.
Freire said: "Some people believe the market is expensive. Historically it is at a high level, but we never had interest rates and inflation as low as now."
Raul Marques of Lisbon broker Tottafundos said the present lull was understandable as some investors would wait for 1996 results and dividends before deciding where to invest.
"We're in a phase of pre-results and pre-dividends. The present calm makes sense," he said.
"After the results come out investors will probably start re-arranging their portfolios," he added.
Analysts said the strong performance of other emerging markets, such as Greece and Turkey, had distracted the attention of some investors away from the Lisbon bourse.
The Greek bourse has risen 25 percent since the start of the year and the Turkish market 62 percent.
